title: HAPTIC DREAMS: SATURDAY KINGDOM
dek: A football game translated into touch, movement, and a world that remembers.
body:
Haptic Dreams begins from the idea that a football game already has a language. A run climbs. A pass crosses. A turnover reverses expectation. A field goal rings three times. A touchdown recruits the whole body. If those phrases remain consistent, a person can begin to recognize the game through touch rather than wait for another screen to explain it.

Saturday Kingdom sends the same selected play sequence into a second output. Michigan and Ohio State begin as two nearly empty strongholds. Possession carries Jon Snow's KansasDAO Art Deco Train across the field. Scores construct towers and light districts. Interceptions reverse the road. Missed kicks dissolve in the sky. The final whistle leaves one completed world behind.

The replay uses eighteen selected events from Michigan's 13-10 win at Ohio Stadium on November 30, 2024. ESPN's play-by-play supplies the sequence, clock, scoring, yardage, and possession; Ohio State's official box score supplies a second record of the game. This is a sourced editorial replay, not a live score feed.

Three views share one event grammar: WORLD shows the cumulative Saturday, SLEEVE demonstrates an eight-zone tactile phrase, and TRANSLATION keeps the original play, haptic phrase, and mythic event visible together. Generated sound is optional. Supported devices can vibrate. A browser-local broadcast channel lets two open tabs follow the same selected play without creating an account or sending personal data.

The important distinction recovered from the early Haptic Dreams conversations is that this is a language, not an effect. The next hardware question is therefore not whether a sleeve can vibrate. It is whether someone can identify run, pass, turnover, score, and miss without seeing the screen.

Concept: Michael Hoydich / Haptic Dreams. Art Deco Lion and Train: Jon Snow for KansasDAO. Interaction translation: Codex / OpenAI for PointCast.
